scope: Theorem 8.1 (Uniform upper bound) of the manuscript “Finite-Circle Obstructions, Binary Codes, and Histogram Embeddings for Edit Distance” (preprints/Finite-Circle-Obstructions-Binary-Codes-and-Histogram-Embeddings-for-Edit-Distance-September-27-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 099 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 8b30fa34409155e6), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 25. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There are absolute constants C > 0 and d0 ≥ 3 such that, for every finite alphabet Σ with |Σ| ≥ 2 and every integer d ≥ d0, there are an integer M ≥ 1 and a deterministic map F : Σ≤d −→ ℓM 1 satisfying ED(x, y) ≤ ∥F(x) − F(y)∥1 ≤ exp (︁ C √︁ log d log log d )︁ ED(x, y) (x, y ∈ Σ≤d ). Here ℓM 1 is real, and both C and d0 are independent of Σ.
